versions.provenance: 8th edition esophagus and esophagogastric junction (EGJ) staging, rewritten from criteria published on Medscape/public references; interim content pending the licensed content and R1 clinical verification.
versions.introduction:
8th edition staging covers carcinomas of the esophagus and esophagogastric junction (EGJ), and its defining feature is that it separates them into three distinct stage-grouping schemes: clinical (cTNM, before treatment), pathologic (pTNM, after resection without neoadjuvant therapy), and post-neoadjuvant (ypTNM, after preoperative therapy plus resection). Squamous cell carcinoma and adenocarcinoma have different clinical and pathologic stage tables, and for early node-negative tumors the pathologic group also depends on histologic grade (and, for squamous cell carcinoma, tumor location). The stageGroups below list the PATHOLOGIC (pTNM) anatomic groups for both histologies, and the postNeoadjuvant block holds the separate ypTNM table.

N is defined by the NUMBER of involved regional nodes rather than their location (N1 = 1 to 2, N2 = 3 to 6, N3 = 7 or more). A key nuance is the anatomic split at the EGJ: a tumor with its epicenter within 2 cm of the cardia (Siewert I to II) is staged as esophageal, whereas an epicenter more than 2 cm into the stomach is staged as gastric. Response to neoadjuvant therapy (captured by the yp table) and completeness of resection are important prognostic factors.

t.label: High-grade dysplasia, defined as malignant cells confined to the epithelium by the basement membrane
Tumor invades the lamina propria, muscularis mucosae, or submucosa
T1a: Tumor invades the lamina propria or muscularis mucosae
T4a: Tumor invades the pleura, pericardium, azygos vein, diaphragm, or peritoneum
T4b: Tumor invades other adjacent structures such as the aorta, vertebral body, or airway

n.label: Regional lymph nodes cannot be assessed
N1: Metastasis in 1 to 2 regional lymph nodes
N2: Metastasis in 3 to 6 regional lymph nodes
N3: Metastasis in 7 or more regional lymph nodes

postNeoadjuvant.note: Applied after neoadjuvant therapy; uses ypT, ypN, ypM. In 8th edition the yp stage groups are identical for squamous cell carcinoma and adenocarcinoma (unlike the clinical and pathologic tables).

versions.regionalNodes: Regional lymph nodes extend from periesophageal cervical nodes to the celiac nodes and include paraesophageal, paratracheal, subcarinal, diaphragmatic, paracardial, left gastric, common hepatic, splenic, and celiac nodes. N is defined by the NUMBER of involved regional nodes, not their anatomic location.
versions.histologicGrade: GX (not assessable), G1 (well differentiated), G2 (moderately differentiated), G3 (poorly differentiated or undifferentiated). For early node-negative tumors, grade participates in the pathologic stage grouping.
versions.histopathologicTypes: Squamous cell carcinoma (predominant in the upper and middle esophagus) and adenocarcinoma (predominant in the lower esophagus and esophagogastric junction, often arising in Barrett esophagus). The two histologies use separate pathologic stage-group tables.
prognosticFactors: Depth of invasion (T) and number of involved regional lymph nodes (N)
Histologic type (squamous cell carcinoma vs adenocarcinoma)
Histologic grade (particularly for early node-negative tumors)
Tumor location for squamous cell carcinoma (upper/middle vs lower)
Response to neoadjuvant therapy (ypTNM) and completeness of resection; lymphovascular invasion
